raw_provenance_object.plain_explanation: If you leave your job, you promise not to work for or start a competing business anywhere in India for the next 12 months. This restriction applies to any business that competes with your current employer.
raw_provenance_object.legal_assessment: This clause is a post-employment non-compete agreement. Under Indian law, agreements that prevent a person from exercising a lawful profession or business after their employment ends are generally void and unenforceable. While restrictions during active employment are valid, this specific 12-month post-termination ban is likely illegal.
raw_provenance_object.recommended_action: Ask to remove this clause entirely, as it is likely unenforceable. If the company insists on keeping it, consult a lawyer to understand the specific risks, but be aware that Indian courts typically strike down such post-employment restraints.
raw_provenance_object.consequence: the clause is likely unenforceable, but the company could still try to use it to threaten you or stop you from finding new work

claims.claim: Agreements that restrain a person from exercising a lawful profession, trade, or business after employment ends are void under Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872.

cited_sources.title: Agreement in restraint of trade, void
cited_sources.text:
Agreement in restraint of trade, void.—Every agreement by which any one is restrained from
exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind, is to that extent void.
_Exception_ 1.—Saving of agreement not to carry on business of which good-will is sold.—One
who sells the good-will of a business may agree with the buyer to refrain from carrying on a similar business, within specified local limits, so long as the buyer, or any person deriving title to the good-will from him, carries on a like business therein, provided that such limits appear to the Court reasonable, regard being had to the nature of the business.
